speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger in detail, including when it started and what makes it better or worse. To help narrow this down, have you noticed any joint deformity, warmth, or a visible lump in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That mechanism of injury sounds like a fracture or tendon avulsion. Did you hear a "pop" or "snap" at the moment of impact? Also, can you actively extend and flex your finger, and is the pain located at the tip, middle, or base of the finger? REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Right Hand.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Extensor Tendon Avulsion).

The X-ray rules out a bony fracture, and the history of hyperextension while playing football combined with swelling at the distal interphalangeal joint is classic for this injury. Can you confirm if you are unable to straighten the tip of your finger?

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
